newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midco unleaded, diesel track NYMEX lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midco unleaded, diesel track NYMEX lower.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded gasoline and diesel prices eased on Monday, tracking plunging NYMEX front-month futures lower on steady differentials, traders said.
"Everything followed the Merc," one trader said of the futures market, which saw February unleaded close down 2.27 cents a gallon and front-month heating oil end off 2.45 cents a gallon on the day.
Despite the plunging futures prices, spot differentials in Chicago and Group Three were largely unchanged. But traders said basis should open higher on Tuesday to reflect the lower futures prices.
The Williams Pipeline Co confirmed it would not accept additional nominations on January shipments to the Group Three market in the lower Midwest because of high system inventories.

The Williams pipeline system, which moves refined product from Midwest and Gulf Coast refiners into Group Three, reported 1.36 million barrels of high sulphur diesel, 6.63 million barrels of N-grade 87 octane unleaded gasoline and 753,000 barrels of premium unleaded on hand.
"The system is full, and storage is full," one trader said.

Traders said bitter winter temperatures in the Midwest were expected to cut gasoline demand but could revive heating oil demand as consumers call local heating oil suppliers to refill home heating oil tanks.
"(Consumers) have consumed all they have at home, and jobbers will be making the rounds again in the next couple of weeks," one Chicago-area trader said.
Chicago jet/kero firmed to bids 0.75 cent a gallon above NYMEX February heating oil, and remained 4.25 cents under the print in Group Three.
Diesel and unleaded differentials were largely unchanged in the Chicago and Group Three markets.
